$comment: The contract inventory. Spec Testing item 1, implementation Task 0.5.
THE GATE IS THIS FILE, NOT THE ASSERTION TOTAL. The spike settled that
empirically rather than by argument: tools/scoring.test.mjs reported
`1535 passed, 0 failed` while running against a public suffix list that had
been silently swapped underneath it, and the count was byte-identical to the
correct baseline. A number that cannot notice that is not a coverage signal.
So: every area below must have a passing suite; the total is REPORTED beside
it as a tripwire; and no entry is removed without a stated replacement.
A decrease in a suite's count must name the assertions removed and where the
Enforced by tests/contract/inventory.test.mjs, which runs each suite and
compares what it printed against what is recorded here.

baseline.note: The pre-refactor total, from the spec's baseline table. Reproduced on 2026-08-27.

suites.note: Reports findings rather than an assertion count, which is why it has no number. Stays in npm test: it is the only thing that catches js/locales-en.js drifting from locales/en.json, and Phase 2 changes that file's format.

notInNpmTest.why: The five-surface comparison against the committed baseline. 38 s for 30 cases, so it runs at every phase gate rather than inside npm test. Framework §3's 'move it to every commit' reading was based on an 8-case corpus and was revised when the corpus was completed.
areas: five-surface equivalence against v0.5.0: result, query trace, CSV, HTML report, DOM

notInNpmTest.why: Regenerates the measured coverage columns of tests/state-matrix.json. Run when the corpus or the registry changes; state-matrix.test.mjs is what gates the result.
areas: corpus coverage measurement

notInNpmTest.why: Live DNS. A local grade-DISTRIBUTION check and never a gate, never the equivalence oracle.
